hook.line: This is what most people do when using ChatGPT.
hook.visual: Man in a navy wide-brim hat and glasses talks to camera, mic visible; white title box 'Let ChatGPT Write Your Prompt for You' over his chest.

beats.what: Calls out the common mistake: typing a general question into ChatGPT
Cut to the ChatGPT app screen recording under his face, typing 'how do I create a monthly budget'
Generic answer shown on screen while he says general question gives general answer
Back to full face, holding phone: 'the trick is' reveal of letting ChatGPT rewrite the prompt
Screen shows 'make the following a better prompt' and ChatGPT's refined prompt
Improved prompt shown as a quote card, then pasted into a new chat
Structured step-by-step budget answer scrolls under his face: 'see the difference?'
Budget breakdown table as the payoff, then use cases listed
Full face close: try it and tell me what you think

why_it_works: Before/after on the same budget question, so the viewer sees the gap between a generic and a structured answer
The trick is a single copyable line, also put in the caption, so it is easy to save and try
Phone screen sits in the lower half with his face kept on top, so the explainer never leaves the frame
weaknesses: Hook names a familiar habit rather than showing the better result first
No word-by-word captions; long screen recordings with small text are hard to read on a phone
Quiet mix (measured -37.6 LUFS) with no music bed
for_robert: Use the face-on-top, screen-below split for a before/after prompt demo; Fred could point at the 'after' answer when it lands.
